h: The first card FurMark famously frightened
f: Geeks3D says its VRM was undersized for FurMark and OCCT loads.
AMD added a Catalyst 8.8 check keyed on the file name FurMark.exe, then a texture-to-ALU ratio check in 9.8.
A small monitoring chip watches the voltage regulators and throttles one PowerPlay level when they overload.
FurMark 1.8.2 at 1080p: 6478 points (108 FPS).
FurMark 1.9.0 at 1080p: 1769 points (29 FPS) on the same card.
In FurMark: 153 W with the limiter, 304 W without (TechPowerUp, quoted by Geeks3D).
The limiter engaged only when the driver detected FurMark or OCCT.
ASUS left the power limiter off its card, so FurMark ran at full speed in JeGX's review.
Forum users report 15,723 to 17,826 points at 4K Optimized (different systems).
A third-party listing shows 18,035 points (301 FPS) at the 1080p preset.
Both fit roughly 60 points per FPS: the score is frames rendered in a 60-second run.
366 W in FurMark at 1440p, and Tom's Hardware said AMD's new cards 'throttle more than just about any other GPU we've tested recently'.
Superposition 4K Optimized: 39,406 on a Core i9-13900K (forum report).
Superposition 8K Optimized on liquid nitrogen: 17,657 (HWBot snapshot).
CENS: 3.825 GHz with 3D stability, validated in Superposition 8K, 18,701 points.
FurMark 1080p preset: 37,387 points (623 FPS), third-party listing.
FurMark 2.5.0.0 (26 Dec 2024) added support for both cards.
Cached Hall of Fame pages show RTX 5090 systems in the high 40,000s; one snapshot lists 47,311 with a Core i9-14900KS at rank 85. Standings change constantly.
